newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus shares rebound after marginal declines.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus shares rebound after marginal declines.

text.p: Cyprus equities closed the week 0.45 percent higher on a renewed buying spree in the last three days of the week after marginal declines that spanned seven consecutive days.
The 43-share Cyprus Stock Exchange (CSE) index closed the week at 75.22 points, up from 74.88 points recorded last week.
The market did not test the low of 73.90 points reached on January 31. Brokers said it was early to talk about a resistance level.
"It would be too risky to say a resistance level has been formed," said one analyst, who warned against sudden rises as an impulse reaction to declines.
"Gradual rises after declines show a more mature market."
Laiki Investments, a subsidiary of the Cyprus Popular Bank forecast the price/earnings ratio of the market at 12.76 times in 1997, down from about 19 recorded in 1996.
In March the P/E ratio of the bourse was estimated at about 15. Laiki Investments said it believed the P/E ratio of the bourse is currently at its lowest levels since 1994.

"Assuming that economic conditions do improve, interest rates drop further and liquidity levels remain high, we believe that the investor with a medium to long-term investment horizon should perceive the stock market as an attractive investment opportunity," Laiki Investments said.
Of the seven sub-indices, four rose. The approved investment index rose 2.9 percent, and banking stocks by 0.63 percent.
Bank of Cyprus shares were trading at 295 on Friday, dropping half a cent. Bank of Cyprus nil paid rights shares started trading on the bourse on Monday at 93.5 cents.
They were trading at 94.5 cents at the end of the week.
The Cyprus Popular Bank gained 4.5 cents and was trading at 298.5. The Hellenic Bank gained five cents, at 279.5, and Universal Savings Bank was trading at 181 cents, up a cent from last week.
Universal Life Insurance was up 2.5 cents, trading at 460.5 on Friday while Interamerican Insurance was up one cent to 93.5.
Blue-chip cement manufacturer Vassiliko was up two cents at 156.5 and Cyprus Cement was down 8.5 cents to 249.5.
Shares of beer-maker KEO were trading for 103.5, up one cent from last week.
National carrier Cyprus Airways was trading at 29.25 cents from 28.8 cents last week.
